products.notice: Sold to adults 18+. The Claude lessons are for adults; this course never asks a child to use Claude.

faq.q: Can my child use Claude?
faq.a: No. Claude is for adults 18 and over, and you may not share your account with anyone, including your children. In these courses, only an adult ever types or speaks to Claude. If a child has an idea, they tell you or write it on paper, and you type it in your own words. Never put a child's name, face, voice, school or photos into any AI tool.

faq.q: Do I need to pay for Claude?
faq.a: No. Every lesson in Safe and Simple AI 60+, and the core of Everyday AI for Adults, works on Claude's free plan. One optional lesson in the adult course (5.7, on agents that take action) covers features that need a paid Claude plan, and it says so.

faq.q: Do I need to pay for n8n?
faq.a: Not to follow the course. n8n offers a free 14-day cloud trial, and a free edition you can run on your own computer. Check n8n's current prices before you choose a paid plan.

faq.q: Is this legal, medical or financial advice?
faq.a: No. The courses teach you to use AI for questions, and to take decisions to a doctor, pharmacist, lawyer, bank or adviser.

faq.q: I bought this for my parent. Can they use my account?
faq.a: No. Claude accounts can't be shared. They set up their own free account, on their own phone, in Lesson 3.1. You can sit next to them while they do it.

faq.q: What format are the files?
faq.a: PDF, sized for US Letter paper. Everyday AI for Adults comes as a zip with the PDF, a folder of n8n workflow files (JSON) and a Claude Skill. Open the PDFs on a phone, tablet or computer, or print them. For Safe and Simple AI 60+, printing is recommended.

faq.q: Why are some lessons dated?
faq.a: Apps, screens and prices change. Lessons that depend on them say when they were last checked. If your screen looks different, the lesson tells you what to look for.

products.summary: Four n8n automations for a local business that draft, never send: a site health check, a lead-form reply, a missed-call text-back and a review request, with a guide that explains every node.
products.intro: A written guide and four importable n8n workflow files, by Miro. Each workflow checks its input, writes the lead, call, job or site status to a plain text file on your own machine, and drafts the reply for you to send. Nothing is sent by the files, and nothing needs an account, a key or a password. Import them in an afternoon, test them with made-up data, and keep the owner in the loop.

Send every customer the same review request after a job, written while the job is fresh, with no cherry-picking.
Learn the five habits that make these workflows safe to adapt: untrusted input, 400 on bad data, draft never send, no secrets in the files, a fenced machine.

faq.q: Are the workflow files really tested?

products.cover_alt: Cover of The Family AI-Scam Defense Workbook: white type on plum with marigold concentric arcs, and three labels: Safe word, Callback rule, By the phone.
products.summary: A household plan you make in one sitting: a family safe word, a callback rule, a never-paste list, practice drills, and the pages you keep by the phone. A plan before the phone rings.
products.intro: A printable workbook, by Miro. AI tools can now copy a voice, make up a video and write a message with no mistakes in it, so the old clues are not much help. This workbook does not try to teach you to spot fakes. It gives your family a few simple moves that still work when the fake is perfect: stop, hang up, call back on a number you already know. You read it together at the kitchen table, fill in the boxes with a pen, practise twice, and put the cards up.
benefits: Choose a family safe word the right way, and agree that asking for it is never rude.
Hang up on any call that asks for money, a code or personal details, and call back on a number you wrote down while you were calm.
Keep one clear list of what never goes into an AI tool, a text or a phone call.
Check any unexpected call, text, email or video against six stop signs on one page.
Open the conversation with an older parent without it sounding like "you are getting old", and set their phone corner up in one visit.
Run short, announced family drills so the words are already there when you need them.
Know who to contact, in what order, if a scam gets through, with the official reporting sites and helplines already printed and your own numbers filled in.

faq.a: No. It does not teach any app. It is a plan for what your family does when a call or message asks for money, a code or personal details.

faq.q: Will it stop my family being scammed?
faq.a: It can't promise that, and it doesn't. What it gives you is a plan made ahead of time: a word, a callback list, a few sentences you have already said out loud, and a page that tells you who to call.

faq.q: How is it different from Safe and Simple AI 60+?
faq.a: The course teaches an older adult to use Claude on a phone. This workbook teaches no app at all: it is the household plan. Some safety advice appears in both, because it is the same advice from the same official sources. If you have the course, the new material here is Parts 6, 7 and 9 and the fuller reporting steps in Part 8.

faq.q: Are the drills trick calls?
faq.a: No. Every drill is announced and starts with "This is a drill." The ground rules say never to test anyone with a call they are not expecting.

faq.q: Where do the phone numbers and reporting steps come from?
faq.a: From the official pages of the FTC, the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center, the Department of Justice's National Elder Fraud Hotline and AARP, each read on 5 Oct 2026. Part 10 lists every page. Details change, so the workbook tells you to trust the official site if it differs.

faq.q: Does it print in black and white?
faq.a: Yes. The pages you write on use outline boxes with a dark title bar, and every page was checked as a grey image.

faq.q: Is it legal advice?
faq.a: No. It is general information for households. Parts 6 and 8 say so on the page.

products.intro: A course by Miro on the three lanes he runs himself, with his own agent, ATLAS, doing the repetitive parts. You learn to cut clips only from footage you're allowed to use, to build and sell one product from something you already know, and to open a one-product store with a supplier you've tested. Each lesson ends with one thing to do. No figure for what you'll earn appears anywhere in it.
benefits: Join a clipping campaign that supplies its footage, read its rules as a checklist, and find, cut and caption the moments worth posting.
Turn something you've actually done into one guide, kit or short course, with the model as your editor, and test it as a stranger would.
Write a product page that describes what's inside, with counted numbers and nothing invented.
Take payment with a link and deliver files only after the payment provider confirms the purchase.
Open a store around one product you've handled yourself: sample ordered, delivery timed, your own photos.
Run all of it from one weekly report where every number has a source and a time, or says unknown.

products.notice: Sold to adults 18+. The course teaches methods and describes what the author does; it doesn't promise income or results.

faq.q: Is this a video course or an ebook?
faq.a: Both exist, with the same lessons: one narrated video per lesson, or one PDF, or both together. Choose on this page.

faq.q: Will this tell me how much I'll make?
faq.a: No. The course contains no earnings figures. It teaches three methods and how to read your own numbers from their sources.

faq.q: Do I need to pay for tools?
faq.a: No subscription is needed to follow the lessons. Claude's free plan covers the writing, the video tool used for cutting is free, and a payment account charges per sale.

faq.q: Is clipping other people's videos allowed?
faq.a: Only with permission. Module 1 is built on one rule: cut only footage the owner has put up for clippers, with the campaign's rules saved.

faq.q: Do I have to do all three?
faq.a: No. The modules stand alone, and the last lesson helps you pick one lane for your first month.

faq.q: How do I get it?
faq.a: After payment you land on your access page with your download. Bookmark it; it makes fresh download links each time you open it.
